mechanism_narrative: Higher levels of total non-farm employment (PAYEMS) indicate strong labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS is below its 5-year moving average, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of negative returns is <= 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 2.0%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.0%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of negative returns is <= 40%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a decline in residential fixed investment (RSAFS) indicates a weakening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% in the past month, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of positive returns is <= 40%).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0), the economy is in an expansion phase, and S&P 500 forward returns are positive over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 105.0, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of negative returns is <= 40%).

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand for residential construction, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and supports equity market performance, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When HOUST is below its 12-month moving average, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of negative returns is <= 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.0%, it signals economic weakness and reduced consumer spending, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE > 4.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of positive returns is <= 40%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% indicates a tightening monetary policy and rising inflation, which together predict negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% and CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of positive returns is <= 40%).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0), the economy is in a contraction phase, and S&P 500 forward returns are negative over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 95.0, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for the hypothesis that the proportion of positive returns is <= 40%).
